name: Desert Containment
description: This chapter introduces the Desert Containment multiplayer game environment as a novel research testbed for investigating coordination, leadership, and performance dynamics in human-agent teams. Designed to simulate real-time collaborative tasks under uncertainty and role asymmetry, Desert Containment enables experimentation with both human and artificial operator roles, guiding ground players through a distributed search-and-containment mission. Through a series of studies—including fully human teams, Wizard-of-Oz simulations, autonomous AI agents, and competitive multi-team scenarios—the testbed supports rigorous evaluation of team and leadership communication strategies, performance metrics, sub-role differentiation, and operational effectiveness under varying levels of communication and command-and-control (C2) difficulties. We describe the motivation and design process of the testbed, the implementation of key dynamical measures (e.g., team situational awareness, operator appropriateness, containment rate, communication density), and its utility for testing and optimising AI agents for human-AI teaming. This chapter concludes with a discussion of future applications and offers recommendations for leveraging the Desert Containment platform as an open, extensible resource for advancing research on complex human-AI collaboration in high-pressure C2 environments.
